title: The Great Puddle Census
skyStory: The crescent has shrunk to a fifth of itself and is still in Aquarius, sorting the clouds into committees. April in Atlantic Canada has delivered its finest product: puddles, in quantity. The moon has volunteered to count them. Saturn says this is not a real job. The moon has already reached four hundred and twelve and refuses to stop.

reading: Mud season has arrived at the cabin, and the boots by the door look like they lost a wrestling match. That is fine. Mud is just earth that is excited about spring, and you know a thing or two about being excited about everything at once.

The [[Knight of Wands]] asks you to aim your fire at a single task today, ideally one that has been sitting in a drawer since February. Open the drawer. Look it in the eye. Finish one honest piece of it before 3 pm and leave the rest folded for tomorrow. When someone asks how your day went, give them a one-word answer and watch them try to decode it.
joel.mission: Step in exactly one puddle on purpose today, with full commitment, like a kid who has never heard of socks.
joel.omen: A worm crossing a sidewalk. It means slow progress still counts, so keep inching toward the thing.

reading: The shore smells like thaw today, salt and wet stone and something green getting ideas. Stand still for a moment and let it register. A Capricorn knows that seasons turn whether or not anyone signs the paperwork.

Someone near you will be stuck on a problem around mid-afternoon, and you will see the answer the way a Wood Rat sees a crumb under the couch. Do not hand it over. Ask them one perfect question instead and watch their face light up as they find it themselves. Leveling people up is your favourite sport, and today you score from the sidelines.
nancy.mission: Find the biggest puddle on your route and give it a dignified name, then use that name in conversation later.
nancy.omen: A crow riding a swaying power line like it is nothing. Balance is easier than it looks, so stop overthinking the next step.

together.text: Send each other a photo of the muddiest thing you see today, no caption. Score it out of ten for drama. Saturn will claim to be above this contest but secretly keeps the spreadsheet, and the moon has bet on Nancy.
